 Order

Petitioners have filed this petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code for quashing of FIR dated 09.08.2017 registered at Crime No. 483/2017 at Police Station Itarsi, District Hoshangabad (M.P.) for offences under Sections 406, 417, 418, 420, 421, 422, 423, 465, 467, 468 and 477A of Indian Penal Code.

2. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that due to mistake in a cheque,
which was given by petitioners to complainant/respondent No.2, in figures correct amount of Rs.
11,41,046/- was mentioned but in words "eleven thousand forty one thousand forty six only"
has been mentioned.
It is submitted that later on petitioners had paid the complete amount through RTGS.
Grievance of respondent No.2 has been addressed.
Notices has been issued to respondent No.2 and despite service of notice, respondent No.2 has not appeared.
Court has proceeded exparte against respondent No.2.
It is submitted that respondent No.2 has filed a criminal case to settle the civil disputes.
From charge-sheet, which is filed by police, it is clear that petitioners and respondent No.2 was having business dealings with each other for long time.
Some money was required to be paid by the petitioners which was not paid and cheque which was given was defective, therefore, same could not be encashed.
It is submitted that act of petitioners in giving cheque does not amount to cheating.
There was a civil dispute between the parties and complainant ought to have file a civil suit for recovery.

Moreover, on going through documents that has been filed by the petitioners alongwith application for amendment, it is found in seizure memo which has been prepared by police, it has been mentioned that complete amount has been paid.
In view of aforesaid submissions, learned Senior Counsel appearing for petitioners made a prayer for quashing of FIR lodged against the petitioners.
3. Government Advocate appearing for the respondent No.1/State opposed the petition.

It is submitted that petitioners had intentionally filled up the words wrongly in the cheque and therefore,
cheque could not be encashed.

Petitioners were having guilty intention and they wanted to cheat respondent No.2.
4.
Heard the counsel for the parties.

sentences.text: There was no misrepresentation made by petitioners to respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 has not acted on the misrepresentation and has transferred any money or article to petitioners.
Petitioners and respondent No. 2 were in regular business dealings with each other and some dues were not paid to respondent No.2.
Issuing a wrong cheque or defective cheque will not make out the offence under Sections 406, 417, 418, 420, 421, 422, 423, 465, 467, 468 and 477A of IPC.
Complete amount has also been paid to the complainant.
6. Considering aforesaid circumstances, FIR dated 09.08.2017 registered vide Crime No. 483/2017 at Police Station Itarsi, District Hoshangabad (M.P.) is quashed.
Resultantly, all consequential proceedings are also quashed.
7. Petition is allowed and disposed off.
